core_conclusion: Rotated triangular boundaries create competing stable registry families with opposite directional bias; selecting the lower-energy family reverses the equilibrium prepared response, while the switching location is edge-model sensitive.

caption: Figure 5. Boundary-induced registry-state competition. (a) Zero-force energy differences locate equilibrium crossings of registry families A and B for triangular cuts with edge orientations phi_e=20 deg and 25 deg. (b) The competing families carry opposite branch-followed directional splittings. (c) Selecting the lower-energy family at each fixed twist reverses the prepared-state directional sign at the energy crossing; no dynamical trajectory across the discontinuous family change is implied. (d) Varying the outer-site energy weight shifts the equilibrium switching angle and can move it outside the original 0–3 deg window. The mechanism is therefore registry-state competition, whereas the exact switch angle is edge-model sensitive.
